analysis:
Only a test file changed: provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/ProviderLoop/ClusterPairSlotTests.swift. The head adds an import of DarkbloomClusterProtocol (line 4), a `tensorAssistant` property on ScriptedPairOwner (lines 67-68), and passes it into DistributedResidentReadiness (lines 82-84). It also adds a new test, aPairWithTheResidentAssistantReportsItsMTPPosture (lines 182-198). That test checks that slot MTP posture (configured/active/rounds) follows pair readiness when a resident assistant is loaded, and stays disabled otherwise.

No production code is in this unit. Nothing here touches the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-011), key custody, prompt encryption, or fan helper boundaries. The scripted owner is test-only, with no process, model or GPU. The test uses hard-coded fixture hashes and no secrets.

The production side of the change (how readiness.tensorAssistant is consumed and how bridge.mtpStatusSnapshot is reported to the coordinator) is outside the supplied evidence. Next-pass reviewers should confirm that the self-reported MTP/assistant fields in heartbeat or capacity data stay advisory. They must not influence routing trust, attestation, or authorization beyond the existing gates, and the added assistant policy/inventory hash must not widen what a provider can claim. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.
